record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Suppose a plane geometric graph on a finite planar point set has the α-diamond property for some fixed α and also has the d-good polygon property for some fixed d ≥ 1. Can the known general upper bound 8d(π − α)^2/(α^2 sin^2(α/4)) on its spanning ratio be improved to a strictly smaller bound?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7. Can the spanning ratio for plane graphs with the α-diamond property and the d-good polygon property be improved? Specifically, can one show that the spanning ratio is strictly less than 8d(π − α)^2/(α^2 sin^2(α/4))?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the plane, and let $G=(P,E)$ be a plane straight-line graph on $P$ (i.e., a planar graph whose edges are non-crossing straight-line segments between points of $P$). For a parameter $0<\alpha<\pi/2$, say that $G$ has the $\alpha$-diamond property if, for every edge $e=uv\in E$, at least one of the two isosceles triangles having $e$ as base and base angle $\alpha$ (one on each side of $e$) contains no point of $P\setminus\{u,v\}$ in its interior. For a parameter $d\ge 1$, say that $G$ has the $d$-good polygon property if, for every face $F$ of $G$ and every pair of vertices $u,v$ on the boundary of $F$ such that the open segment $uv$ lies in the interior of $F$, the shorter of the two boundary paths from $u$ to $v$ along $\partial F$ has Euclidean length at most $d\cdot\|u-v\|$.

The spanning ratio of $G$ is $\sup_{u\ne v\in P} \frac{d_G(u,v)}{\|u-v\|}$, where $d_G$ denotes shortest-path distance in $G$ using Euclidean edge lengths.

It is known that any such $G$ satisfying both properties has spanning ratio at most
$$\frac{8d(\pi-\alpha)^2}{\alpha^2\sin^2(\alpha/4)}.$$

Question: Can this upper bound be replaced by a strictly smaller function of $\alpha$ and $d$ that still holds for every finite point set $P$ and every plane straight-line graph $G$ on $P$ with the $\alpha$-diamond property and the $d$-good polygon property?
artifact.status_search_result: The known upper bound $8d(\pi-\alpha)^2/(\alpha^2\sin^2(\alpha/4))$ was established as a generalization/slight improvement of Das–Joseph-type bounds for plane graphs with the $\alpha$-diamond and $d$-good polygon properties. Recent searches turn up no published improvement of this constant, and the question is listed as an open problem in the standard survey on plane geometric spanners.

status_evidence.title: On Generalized Diamond Spanners
status_evidence.snippet: A constrained plane graph with the α-visible diamond property and the d-good polygon property is a spanner of the visibility graph with spanning ratio 8d(π-α)^2/(α^2 sin^2(α/4)).
status_evidence.claim: This is the current best general upper bound; no strictly smaller bound has been established.

status_evidence.title: On plane geometric spanners: A survey and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems concerning spanning ratios of plane geometric graphs with the α-diamond and d-good polygon properties.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of improving the bound is explicitly listed as open.
